newsitem.title: USA: Healthdyne says receives acquisition offers. [CORRECTED 15:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Healthdyne says receives acquisition offers. [CORRECTED 15:55 GMT]

text.p: Healthdyne Technologies Inc said Wednesday it has been advised by an unnamed Fortune 500 company that the company has a "strong strategic interest" in acquiring Healthdyne and was prepared to pay a price higher than the $15 per share offered by Invacare Corp.
The company said it has also received indications of interest from other strategic buyers and a financial buyer and intended to continue discussions with the parties.

The company also said that its board, if re-elected at the July 30 annual meeting, will amend the company's bylaws to permit holders of at least 25 percent of the company's common stock to call special shareholder meetings and will amend its shareholder rights plans to allow a bidder who meets certain conditions to call a special meeting of shareholders to vote on a binding resolution to redeem the rights.

Healthdyne further said that, in the event that Invacare's four nominees were elected at the meeting, its board had authorized a $1.0 million trust to be used by the company's continuing directors to pay the expenses associated with any action taken by Invacare or its nominees.

These include an appeal by Invacare against the July 3 district court decision upholding a continuing directors provision of Healthdyne's shareholder rights plan, a provision Invacare was seeking to strike out.

Invacare's $200 million hostile bid for Healthdyne has been repeatedly rejected as inadequate. Invacare is now seeking to elect a simple majority to Healthdyne's board at its annual meeting and has said it will not oppose a minority of three Healthdyne incumbents on the seven-member board.
